claim.claim-text: 1. A flywheel energy storage device, comprising:
2. The flywheel energy storage device according to claim 1, wherein the composite elliptical ovoid shell is mounted on the axial shaft via boss plate attachments on internal boss plate supports.
3. The flywheel energy storage device of claim 1 or claim 2, further comprising a plurality of sets of helical wraps, each set of helical wraps having a uniform width.
4. The flywheel energy storage device of claim 3, wherein each set of helical wraps has a layer extending around the outer surface of the shell and the hub on both sides of the axis of rotation.

5. The flywheel energy storage device of claim 3, wherein each set of helical wraps has a near continuous, single ended filamentary material wound in a unidirectional relationship and encased in a resin matrix.
6. The flywheel energy storage device of claim 3, wherein each set of helical wraps is uniformly stressed over the width of each wrap during rotation.
7. The flywheel energy storage device of claim 3, wherein each set of helical wraps has a radially oriented, layered composite shell.

8. The flywheel energy storage device of claim 3, wherein the helical wraps are disposed in an overlapping relationship with one another on portions of the hub at locations adjacent to the axis of rotation.

9. The flywheel energy storage device of claim 1 or claim 2, wherein each layer of the radially oriented helical wrap is angled initially 5 degrees and stepped to 35 degrees to shift wrap layer mass build-up away from the axis of rotation to increase flywheel moment of inertia.

10. The flywheel energy storage device of claim 1 or claim 2, wherein the radially oriented helical wrap is configured to transfer tensile tip stress to the thickened structure near the axis of rotation under compressive stress, thereby maximizing the effective strength of the filament wound composite laminate.
11. The flywheel energy storage device of claim 1 or claim 2, further comprising integrated internal structures attached to and providing compression support for the external ovoid shell.
12. The flywheel energy storage device of claim 11, wherein:

a) the internal structures are formed from metal or a near continuous single ended filamentary material wound in a unidirectional relationship in a plurality of layers and encased in resin matrix; or b) the internal structures have a minimum inner-to-outer ratio of about 0.1 when compared with the outer diameter of the ovoid shell.

13. The flywheel energy storage device of claim 1 or claim 2, wherein the internal structures are formed from metal, composite laminate wound in a unidirectional relationship in a plurality of layers and that are bonded to the inner layer of the external ovoid shell, optionally wherein the internal structures have a minimum inner-to-outer ratio of about 0.1 when compared with the outer diameter of the ovoid shell.
14. The flywheel energy storage device of claim 1 or claim 2, wherein the width-to-diameter ratio available of the external ovoid is 0.1 to 1.0.
15. The flywheel energy storage device of claim 1 or claim 2, wherein the inner and outermost peripheral surface of the ovoid shell is in the configuration of a rotational ellipse.
